en.name: Saint James, Apostle
en.summary: Honors James, son of Zebedee and brother of John, the first apostle martyred and patron of the Santiago de Compostela pilgrimage.
en.body: This feast honors James, son of Zebedee and brother of John, one of the inner circle of three disciples closest to Jesus alongside Peter and John, present at the Transfiguration and in Gethsemane. He is recorded in the Acts of the Apostles as the first of the Twelve to be martyred, beheaded on the order of King Herod Agrippa I around the year 44. Strong medieval tradition holds that his remains were later transported to northwestern Spain, where the shrine of Santiago de Compostela grew into one of the three great pilgrimage destinations of medieval Christendom alongside Rome and Jerusalem, and the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route to his shrine remains one of the most walked pilgrimage paths in the world today.
